newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait, Canada discuss arm deals, no contracts.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait, Canada discuss arm deals, no contracts.

text.p: Canada's National Defence Minister Douglas Young said on Monday he has discussed potential arms sales with his Kuwaiti countrpart, but no deals were concluded.
"We have discussed a wide range of possibilities," Young told a news confernce before leaving Kuwait after a two-day visit. "But, we did not conclude any specific deal."
"I leave the business to the people who produce the equipment and especially who set the prices," he added.
"The potential areas are from the supply of vehicles, lorries, trucks to various types of air defence systems. There has been discussions about some vessels (also)."
"The Minister of Defence (Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah) has indicated that we will continue to investigate opportunities," said Young, who arrived in Kuwait on Saturdy.
Sheikh Salem said Kuwait wanted to cement its strong ties with Canada. "That could either be (through) buying suitable equipment...or to cooperate in training," he said at the joint news conference.
There would be a programme for Kuwaitis to go and train with the Canadians, said Sheikh Salem.
"Every one understands that it is a very competitive environment, but I am very encouraged," said Young.
Kuwaitis "are going to be looking for the very best equipment they can acquire at the best prices with best support systems, and we feel the Canadians are competitive."
"But, again I am not a salesman. I make sure that our country's interests are put forward," said Young who met the Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah on Sunday.
Canada took part in the U.S.-led multinational force that drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait after a seven-month occupation in 1991.
